recognize_zh: 骨髓抹片中巨噬細胞內充滿大量 2–4 µm、卵圓形、帶透明暈圈並有偏心深染小點的酵母菌（Histoplasma capsulatum），右圖另一巨噬細胞同時吞噬紅血球系細胞（hemophagocytosis）——同時具備組織胞漿菌感染與噬血現象。
features: Macrophages distended by numerous small (2–4 µm) oval intracellular yeasts
Yeasts show a crescent-shaped basophilic nucleus/dot with a surrounding clear halo (pseudocapsule artifact)
Panel B: macrophage containing an engulfed erythroid cell/red cell together with yeasts (hemophagocytosis)
Background of hematopoietic precursors including erythroid and granulocytic cells
No budding hyphae or kinetoplasts identified
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows scattered macrophages packed with numerous small, oval, intracellular yeast forms measuring approximately 2–4 µm, each with an eccentric basophilic chromatin crescent and a clear halo (A). A macrophage in panel B contains a phagocytosed erythroid cell together with yeast forms, indicating hemophagocytosis. No kinetoplasts are seen. Findings are consistent with disseminated histoplasmosis with associated hemophagocytosis, supporting secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis in the appropriate clinical and laboratory context; confirmation by GMS/PAS stain, culture or urine/serum Histoplasma antigen is recommended.

ddx.vs: Leishmania amastigotes have both a nucleus and a rod-shaped kinetoplast and lack a halo, and they do not stain with GMS/PAS.
Talaromyces yeasts are slightly larger, elongated, and divide by fission with a central transverse septum rather than budding.
Tachyzoites are crescent/banana-shaped, lack a halo and are GMS-negative.
Cryptococcus is larger (4–10 µm) with a thick mucicarmine-positive capsule, and Candida shows pseudohyphae with budding.
